research_rationale: Identity: the held Federal Register original (7 FR 3541, PDF page 1; text file EO_9158 of the fr-originals job) is Executive Order 9158, Air Medal, signed by Franklin D. Roosevelt on May 11, 1942 (F. R. Doc. 42-4314, filed May 12, 1942); the number, title and date agree with the register row. The order has one inventory clause covering its three paragraphs. Two held later instruments amend the order and neither ends it. Executive Order 9242-A (signed September 11, 1942; 7 FR 7874) restated the first paragraph so that service in or with the Army, Navy, Marine Corps or Coast Guard qualifies. Executive Order 14085 section 1 (signed October 3, 2022; 87 FR 60541) further amended the first and second paragraphs by striking and inserting words (Armed Forces, Air Force and Space Force, those individuals, approval of the design by the Secretary of Defense, award by the Secretaries of the Army, the Navy and the Air Force or the Secretary of Homeland Security for the Coast Guard when it is not operating as a service in the Navy, and Coast Guard personnel serving under the jurisdiction of the Navy) and added a final paragraph on uniform regulations. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments the clause continues, amended, and each amendment is a later event that records the text before and after. Current law: the held U.S. Code note under 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, part II, chapter 57 (Office of the Law Revision Counsel release point 119-121, edition current through 2026-10-09) prints the order as amended by both instruments and states no ending; the order has no duration, condition or sunset of its own. Route original_plus_bounded_search: the held original, both held later instruments, no own-terms end, and the three bounded searches after reading their coverage notes. The U.S. Code search found one hit, the note above; its edition ends 2026-10-09, so laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected, which is disclosed here and is not a ground to doubt a presidential order that no held source ends. The eCFR search (point in time as of 2026-10-14) found no hit. The Federal Register catalog notes held for this order are an Amended-by note naming EO 9242-A, a See note naming Transfer Order 30 of the Secretary of Defense dated December 10, 1948 (13 FR 8163), and the Amends note under EO 14085; none is a revocation or supersession. The order was unrevoked and operative on 2026-10-14.
savings_reason: No clause ended and nothing was revoked, so there is no ended command whose awards or effects need saving; the order as amended remains the instrument establishing the Air Medal, and the held U.S. Code note prints it as amended by Executive Order 9242-A and Executive Order 14085 without any ending statement.

Executive Order 14085 amended the order in 2022, after that transfer order, and the Code note prints the order after both. The order has no duration, condition or sunset of its own, so no earlier own-terms end exists and no earlier revocation or supersession is held.
scope_check: One clause, the whole text of the order: establishment of the Air Medal with ribbons for meritorious achievement in aerial flight, the design-approval and award authority of the Secretaries and designated commanding officers, and the rule of one medal with bars or devices and posthumous presentation. All three paragraphs concern the same medal and none was separately ended, revoked or partly revoked by a held instrument; the partial amendments by Executive Order 9242-A and Executive Order 14085 changed wording and added a paragraph.
independent_command_check: No independent command in the order was spent or performed once: the establishment of the medal, the award authority and the one-medal rule are standing commands that continue under the order as amended, and Executive Order 14085 changed their wording but not their existence.

Executive Order 14085 section 1(a) (signed October 3, 2022; 87 FR 60541) further amended that same first paragraph by striking and inserting words (Armed Forces, those individuals, Air Force and Space Force, distinguish themselves) and did not strike the words that Executive Order 9242-A added, so the amendment's wording is carried in the current text. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments the clause continues, amended; the later amendment is recorded as a later event with the text before and after.
